title: Build a white-label usage limits dashboard
description: Verify the usage limits APIs against your workspace with a Client API token, then run a white-label dashboard that sets organization, default per-person, and individual AI spend limits. A labeled sample mode runs without credentials.
prerequisites: The complete Glean backend origin shown under Server instance (QE)
Workspace billing permissions: billing read to view and evaluate limits, billing edit to change them. The ADMIN role alone does not grant them
A user-scoped Client API token with the ADMIN_USAGE and PEOPLE scopes, created by that user in Token Management

demoQueries.expectedBehavior: Lists organization, default per-person, and individual limits per spend client with their threshold actions. The workspace premium-model policy and all thresholds are read-only.

demoQueries.query: Open a person and evaluate their budget
demoQueries.expectedBehavior: Shows the tightest headroom, each applicable rule's cap and used amount, whether the person's own budget or a shared pool causes a warning or block, and any active premium-model restriction.

demoQueries.query: Add a personal override, then remove it
demoQueries.expectedBehavior: Previews the exact upsert before applying it, applies it only after writes are explicitly enabled, and resets it by natural key so the person inherits the default again.

codeAssets.description: Node server and browser UI that read people and departments through @gleanwork/api-client, call the experimental usage limit operations and the OAuth client list through a narrow REST bridge, and test both with Vitest and MSW

steps.title: Install dependencies
steps.description: Installs the pinned Glean SDK, plus Vitest and MSW for the tests. Run the remaining commands from this directory.

steps.title: Run the fixture tests
steps.description: Runs the Vitest suite without credentials or network access. It drives the real SDK and REST bridge against MSW handlers; it is not live verification.

steps.title: Add your backend and token
steps.description: Copy the example, then open .env yourself. Set GLEAN_SERVER_URL to your backend origin and GLEAN_API_TOKEN to a user-scoped Client API token with the ADMIN_USAGE and PEOPLE scopes from Token Management, created by a user with billing permissions. Never paste the token into chat, a command, or a committed file. Leave GLEAN_ENABLE_WRITES=false.

steps.title: Verify against your workspace
steps.description: Makes read-only requests: people, departments, gateway OAuth clients, the limit list, and an organization and personal evaluation. It never writes a policy and exits non-zero when a required API is missing, forbidden, or unavailable.

steps.title: Start the dashboard
steps.description: Open the Local URL printed by the server in your own browser. Writes are off; to change limits on a workspace you are authorized to modify, set GLEAN_ENABLE_WRITES=true in .env and restart. Run npm run demo instead for the fictional sample.

run.url: the Local URL printed by the server

architecture.label: Local Node server
architecture.caption: the token never reaches the browser

aiPrompt: Scaffold and run the usage-admin-dashboard recipe exactly as written. Install with npm ci and run npm run verify:fixture. Copy .env.example to .env, then have the user enter GLEAN_SERVER_URL and GLEAN_API_TOKEN in .env themselves; never ask for, print, or pass the token. The token is a user-scoped Client API token with the ADMIN_USAGE and PEOPLE scopes, and that user needs workspace billing permissions; the ADMIN role alone is not enough. Run the read-only npm run verify, then start npm start and have the user open the printed Local URL in their own browser. The token stays in the local server. Use @gleanwork/api-client 0.20.18 for people and departments. Call the usage limit, reset, and evaluation endpoints and the OAuth client list through the shipped REST bridge, which sends X-Glean-Include-Experimental: true. Live writes stay off unless the user explicitly authorizes changes to that workspace and sets GLEAN_ENABLE_WRITES=true; never retry a write automatically. Saves omit actions so existing thresholds survive. Never synthesize department, IdP-group, model, or org-subtree limits from per-user writes, and never fall back to sample data when a live call fails. The sample dashboard from npm run demo is fictional and does not count as verification.
llmContext: Limits are keyed by target, whose client_id is the spend client, and period. Edit ORGANIZATION, DEFAULT_USER, and USER policies with the single public upsert; omit actions so existing thresholds survive, and reset by natural key. DEFAULT_USER with client_id * is the actions-only premium-model policy; show it read-only. Evaluate a concrete ORGANIZATION or USER with client_id and period; read headroom from effective_limits, causes from decision_causes, and model allowlists from restrictions. Use ai_gateway.usage_client_id verbatim, the glean constant, or an exact typed client ID. Never combine USD and CREDITS. Department and IdP-group limits are not supported. Live unavailability never falls back to fixtures. Manager links are not team membership.

content.problem: Administrators need a customer-branded way to decide who can spend how much on which AI clients, and to see why a person is warned or blocked. This recipe builds that on the usage limits APIs and shows missing capabilities as unavailable rather than inventing policy targets.
takeItFurther: Move the OAuth client list and the usage operations to @gleanwork/api-client once a release covers their current contracts.
Add deployment-specific session authentication and per-admin authorization before hosting this local-only recipe.
Add department and IdP-group limits once the API accepts them as targets.

limitations.title: Preview until a workspace run
limitations.description: Fixture tests cover the API contracts. The recipe stays in preview until an authorized run against a real workspace, including a contained write and reset, passes.

limitations.title: Local single-admin tool
limitations.description: The server binds to loopback and uses one operator’s token. Do not expose it publicly or treat it as a multi-user admin service.

limitations.title: Organization, default, and personal limits only
limitations.description: Department and IdP-group limits are not supported yet. Threshold actions are shown and preserved, not edited. Usage history is not part of this recipe.
